hints: A node's partner sits at the mirrored position. If you could read the second half backwards, the partners would line up side by side.
Find the middle with fast/slow pointers, reverse the second half in place, then walk both halves together and track the maximum pair sum.

1. Move slow 1 and fast 2 steps while fast != null and fast.next != null; slow is now the first node of the second half.
  2. Reverse the list from slow.
  3. Walk p from head and q from the reversed half together.
  4. At each step update best = max(best, p.val + q.val).
  5. Return best.

approaches.name: Copy to an array
approaches.idea: Store values in an array, then check arr[i] + arr[n-1-i] for each i.

approaches.name: Optimal: reverse the second half
approaches.idea: Line partners up by reversing the back half in place.

explain: For 6→2→9→1 the second half 9→1 becomes 1→9. Pairs are (6,1) = 7 and (2,9) = 11, so the answer is 11. With an even length, the slow pointer lands exactly on the second-half start, so both halves have n/2 nodes. Use the reversed half's length to stop the loop.
recognize: Pair the i-th node from the front with the i-th from the back in a linked list → reverse the second half and walk both halves together.
python:
class Solution:
    def pairSum(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> int:
        s = f = head
        while f and f.next: s, f = s.next, f.next.next
        prev = None
        while s: s.next, prev, s = prev, s, s.next
        best = 0
        while prev: best = max(best, prev.val + head.val); prev, head = prev.next, head.next
        return best
javascript: function pairSum(head) { const a = []; for (let c = head; c; c = c.next) a.push(c.val); let b = 0; for (let i = 0; i < a.length / 2; i++) b = Math.max(b, a[i] + a[a.length-1-i]); return b; }
